title: Use a treemap for a budget with many parts in one year.
rule: Draw each part as a rectangle whose area is its amount, largest first, every tile in one light gray with a gap of the page color between tiles, and print each tile’s name, amount and share inside it. The part the title names takes the red point, or the text’s ink where Rule 14.6 sets ink in its place. Fold parts too small to hold their words into one last tile, list each in the table, and say what a negative line the treemap cannot draw leaves out.
use_when: The reader asks where the money in one budget went, the parts number more than a bar chart reads quickly, and the largest few carry the answer.

use_instead.when: The reader compares parts across years
The parts are few or must be ranked exactly
Lines add and take away on the way to a result

text: Area shows the whole and each part’s weight in it at once, and the largest parts claim the most room as they claim the most money. Areas are harder to compare exactly than lengths, so every tile prints its amount and share.
why.basis: Design judgment, from the chart system our founder and editor approved in November 2026

builders: Form treemap: node work/build/chart-kit/oa-chart.mjs build s47; labels.fold_below sets the share under which parts fold, labels.fold_label the folded tile’s name, and labels.point the tile the title names.
